subject: flamingo
pitch: An elegant flamingo standing tall in shallow water. Candy-pink feathers deepening to coral on the wings, with a flash of black flight feathers at the wing tips, an S-curved neck, a bent beak that is pale pink with a black tip, pale yellow eyes and long rose-coloured legs with knobbly knees and webbed feet.
reasoning:
I'm planning the flamingo's proportions and skeleton structure, working out joint positions for the hips, spine, neck, and legs to get realistic scale and pose.

For the neck, I want an S-curve rising from the chest up to the head, so I'm sketching out the control points for that shape. Then I'm thinking through how the body mesh will be lofted along the spine path with varying radii to form the body silhouette.

Still defining beak geometry...

Now I'm placing the eyes as small yellow spheres with black pupils on either side of the head, and starting on the folded wing geometry with joint positions tracing back along the body.

For the wing shape itself, I'm deciding to extrude a flat outline plate rather than sweep a chain, defining the wing as a leaf-shaped silhouette in the back/up plane with coral covert feathers on top and black flight feathers extruded separately underneath.

Shaping the wing's black tips and flight feathers as tapered rod extrusions trailing off the rear outline...

For the wing joint structure, I'm setting up a two-span chain named shoulderL and elbowL, built from a polyline path and parented to the spine chain, rather than relying on a generic "wing" role.

For the tail, I'm planning a short, flat, black-tipped pink tail swept back from the rump using a two-joint chain (tail1, tail2) built from a three-point path extruded with an appropriate orientation.

For legs, I'm positioning hip joints symmetrically at the sides near the base of the body, then building a flamingo-style limb with a hidden thigh, a long upward tibiotarsus, a backward-bending joint mid-leg, and a tarsometatarsus leading down to the foot.

I'll settle on a four-point leg chain—hip, knee, hock, and toe-base—with the knee bowing slightly forward and the hock bending back, which matches the natural leg structure.

For the sweep radius, I'll vary it along the leg length so it's thin overall but bulges near the knobby joints like the hock, using a Gaussian-style bump function, and add small spheres at those joints to accentuate the knobbiness. I'll color the legs a darker rose and taper the radius down toward the foot.

Now I'm placing three forward-facing toes plus a small hallux spike, positioned so they sink slightly into the ground, and connecting webbing slabs between the toes as thin triangular prisms in a lighter pink shade.

I'm also setting up a joint hierarchy for the toes, adding a bone per toe branching from the toe base, mirrored for left and right sides using a suffix convention. Then I'm planning a shallow translucent water disc around the feet, making sure it sits low enough not to float above where the feet touch ground level.

Now I'm adjusting the water cylinder's height and vertical position so it doesn't fully submerge the toes, tweaking the water level and toe geometry so webbing stays slightly visible above the surface, and sketching in thin ripple rings around the feet.

For the body, I'm attaching the water to the root bone so it moves correctly, then laying out loft stations along the spine from tail to neck with varying widths and heights to shape the torso, making sure the body bottom clears the hip height for the legs.

Now I'm designing the neck as an S-curve path using catmull-rom interpolation through several control points, sweeping back then forward then back to give it a natural goose-like bend, ending at the head position, and parenting the neck chain to the spine for proper articulation.

I'm placing the head as a scaled sphere at the neck's tip, then shaping the beak as a tapering path curving downward from inside the head, defining its width and height radii to narrow toward the tip.

For the lower jaw, I'm defining a thinner, shorter path beneath the upper beak, parented to the head with its own joint, then using color bands rather than explicit paint values to shade both beak parts from pink at the base to dark at the tip.

Now I'm placing the eyes as small yellow spheres with black pupils positioned symmetrically on the head, checking their size and offset against the head sphere's radius so they sit naturally embedded in the surface. For the body, I'm picking a candy-pink base color with deeper coral tones for the wings.

Writing gradient and mottle paint definitions...

Positioning the wing plates and flight feathers along the body, tilting the wing axis slightly and setting the body width at the appropriate z-position.

Still working out feather geometry...

Still tuning feather positions...

The wing-plate and feather overlap at the trailing edge works well with the coloring. Now I'm setting up the bone chains, making sure legs parent to root and wings parent to spine2, with leg chains spanning hip, knee, ankle, and toe base joints for both left and right sides.

For the legs I'm sweeping tube geometry with a radius function that bumps thickness near the top, and placing the foot and toe points carefully so the toes sit slightly higher than the ankle. Each toe gets its own joint parented to the toe base, with a spike shape added for claws using a fixed radius.

Between adjacent toes I'm adding flat webbing slabs built from base and tip points, plus a backward-pointing hallux spike for the first toe. Toe directions fan outward based on side (left/right), with varying lengths for outer, middle, and inner toes, and I'm adding small spheres at the knee and hock joints for a knobby look, using a slightly darker color for the leg.

Then I'm layering in blocky icosahedron detailing, ripple rings around the feet using thin torus shapes, and a water cylinder base in a pale teal tone beneath everything. Now I'm setting up the skeleton structure -- defining the root joint, a spine chain built from a curved path with named segments, and a tail chain branching off the first spine bone.

For the tail I'm placing a flat plate bone with an extrusion running backward, giving it a pinkish tone. The body itself is lofted along the spine bone chain with tapering radius toward the tail tip, while the neck is swept along its own chain with a radius function narrowing from a thicker base near the body to a slimmer point at the head, checking that the starting radius matches where it meets the torso.
